course: Skillgrove global graph (EE 105, ME 132, Feedback Systems)

skills.name: Solve a first-order RC low-pass filter in the time domain
Sinusoidal steady state using complex exponentials
Transfer functions, voltage and current gain, transimpedance
Phasors and impedance of R, L, C
Poles and zeros of a transfer function
Conduction in metals, mobility, microscopic Ohm's law
Silicon bond model, electrons and holes
Intrinsic carrier concentration and the mass-action law
Doping with donors and acceptors, carrier concentrations
Diffusion current and the Einstein relation
PN junction in equilibrium: structure and currents
Depletion approximation, fields and depletion width
Qualitative diode I-V: equilibrium, forward, reverse
Minority carrier distribution at junction edges
Diode small-signal model and diffusion capacitance
Solar cells: short-circuit current and open-circuit voltage
MOS capacitor structure and gate contact potential
Fields and potential in oxide and substrate
MOSFET layout, cross section, CMOS and symbols
NMOS regions of operation and observed I-V
Triode region and the MOSFET as a variable resistor
Saturation: pinch-off and the square law
PMOS: regions, sign conventions and small-signal use
Common-source amplifier: transfer curve and bias-point selection
Channel-length modulation and output resistance ro
MOS small-signal model and analysis procedure
MOSFET capacitances CGS, CGD, CDB, CSB
Body effect: threshold shift and gmb
Transistor action, BJT currents and current gain
Forward-active region and the Early effect
Two-port amplifier models and loading in cascades
Isolating bias points, DC versus AC coupling
Common-source gain, input and output impedance
Source follower: gain with body effect and real bias source
Choosing among CS, CG and CD
High load impedance, headroom and gain
Current mirror: ratios and output resistance
Cascode current source and its drawback
Frequency response considerations and coupling capacitors
Cascade frequency response and bandwidth extension
Common-source with a large capacitive load
Differential pair DC bias and large-signal behavior
Differential pair with current mirror load
Loop gain and why feedback helps
Static and dynamic errors in feedback systems
Feedback effect on input and output impedance
Closed-loop stability, gain and phase margins
Open-loop and closed-loop op-amp frequency response
Output swing, slew rate and full-power bandwidth
What feedback does: open vs closed loop
skills.summary: Contrast open-loop and closed-loop control and name the plant, sensor, actuator, controller, reference and disturbance.

skills.name: Block-diagram algebra
skills.summary: Reduce series, parallel and feedback interconnections to a single transfer function.

skills.name: Simple feedback: on-off, P, PI, PID
skills.summary: Compare on-off, proportional, integral and derivative action qualitatively and predict steady-state error.

skills.name: Modeling with differential equations
skills.summary: Write ODE models of mechanical, electrical and fluid elements from physical laws.

skills.name: State-space models
skills.summary: Put an n-th order ODE or coupled ODEs into x'=Ax+Bu, y=Cx+Du form.

skills.name: Cruise control as a feedback example
skills.summary: Model a vehicle speed loop with drag and grade disturbance and see what P and PI control achieve.

skills.name: Laplace transform and its properties
skills.summary: Transform signals and ODEs, use derivative/integral rules and the final value theorem.

skills.name: Modeling methodology: scaling, units, identification
skills.summary: Choose states, nondimensionalize, and pick model fidelity for a control purpose.

skills.name: First-order systems
skills.summary: Find time constant, DC gain, step and free response of a first-order system and its control.

skills.name: Second-order systems: damping and natural frequency
skills.summary: Relate zeta and omega_n to pole locations and to under/over/critically damped responses.

skills.name: Step-response specifications
skills.summary: Compute rise time, overshoot, settling time and steady-state error, and map them to the s-plane.

skills.name: PID control law and its effects
skills.summary: Predict how proportional, integral and derivative gains change the closed-loop poles and errors.

skills.name: Integrator windup and anti-windup
skills.summary: Explain actuator saturation windup and design back-calculation or clamping anti-windup.

skills.name: PID tuning (Ziegler-Nichols and model-based)
skills.summary: Tune a PID from step or ultimate-gain experiments and from a first-order-plus-delay model.

skills.name: PID implementation: derivative filtering, setpoint weighting, discretization
skills.summary: Filter the derivative, weight setpoints and discretize a PID for a computer.

skills.name: Matrix exponential and the general solution
skills.summary: Solve x'=Ax+Bu with e^{At} and the convolution integral.

skills.name: Eigenvalues, modes and diagonalization
skills.summary: Decompose a response into modes using eigenvectors and Jordan form.

skills.name: From state space to transfer function
skills.summary: Compute G(s)=C(sI-A)^{-1}B+D and relate poles to eigenvalues.

skills.name: Realizations: controllable and observable canonical forms
skills.summary: Build a state-space realization from a transfer function; note non-uniqueness.

skills.name: Stability of LTI systems
skills.summary: Decide asymptotic and BIBO stability from eigenvalues or poles; Routh-Hurwitz test.

skills.name: Frequency response of a general LTI system
skills.summary: Get steady-state sinusoidal response from G(j omega) for state-space and TF models.

skills.name: Linear algebra review
skills.summary: Rank, null space, eigenvalues and similarity transforms as used in control.

skills.name: Discrete-time systems and sampling
skills.summary: Model sampled systems as difference equations and check stability inside the unit circle.

skills.name: Loop transfer function and the Gang of Four
skills.summary: Form L=PC and the closed-loop maps S, T, PS, CS from reference, disturbance and noise.

skills.name: Root locus
skills.summary: Sketch how closed-loop poles move with gain using asymptotes, breakaway and angle rules.

skills.name: Nyquist plot and stability criterion
skills.summary: Count encirclements of -1 to infer closed-loop unstable poles.

skills.name: Time delay in feedback loops
skills.summary: Represent delay as e^{-sT}, see its phase lag, and use Padé approximations.

skills.name: Bode's relations and minimum-phase systems
skills.summary: Relate gain slope to phase and recognize nonminimum-phase zeros and delays.

skills.name: Generalized gain, describing functions
skills.summary: Extend gain/phase to nonlinear elements via describing functions and the small-gain idea.

skills.name: Sensitivity functions and disturbance rejection
skills.summary: Use S and T to quantify disturbance attenuation, noise and tracking.

skills.name: Modeling uncertainty
skills.summary: Describe parametric and unmodeled-dynamics uncertainty with additive/multiplicative bounds.

skills.name: Robust stability
skills.summary: Apply the small-gain test |T Δ|<1 and stability margins to uncertain plants.

skills.name: Robust performance
skills.summary: Keep specs under uncertainty using weighted S and T bounds.

skills.name: Feedforward design and 2-DOF control
skills.summary: Add reference and disturbance feedforward to a feedback loop.

skills.name: Frequency-domain performance specifications
skills.summary: Translate bandwidth, peak sensitivity and crossover into design targets.

skills.name: Loop shaping with lead and lag compensators
skills.summary: Shape L(j omega) with lead/lag/PI to meet margins and bandwidth.

skills.name: Fundamental limitations: RHP zeros, delays, Bode integral
skills.summary: Bound achievable bandwidth from RHP poles/zeros and the waterbed effect.

skills.name: Reachability (controllability)
skills.summary: Test reachability with the rank of [B AB ... ] and reach canonical form.

skills.name: State feedback and pole placement
skills.summary: Choose K so that A-BK has desired eigenvalues; Ackermann's formula.

skills.name: Integral action in state feedback
skills.summary: Augment the state with an error integrator to remove steady-state error.

skills.name: Linear quadratic regulator
skills.summary: Pick weights Q, R and interpret the LQR gain trade-off.

skills.name: Observability
skills.summary: Test observability with the rank of [C; CA; ...] and observable canonical form.

skills.name: State estimation with observers
skills.summary: Design an observer gain L so that A-LC is fast and stable.

skills.name: Output feedback and the separation principle
skills.summary: Combine state feedback with an observer and see that the eigenvalues separate.

skills.name: Gaussian random vectors
skills.summary: Mean and covariance of a Gaussian vector, and the covariance of a linear image.

skills.name: Kalman filter
skills.summary: Predict and update a linear state estimate and its covariance for a model with process and measurement noise.

skills.name: Kalman filter as an optimal observer
skills.summary: Choose the linear correction that minimizes the variance of the state error.

skills.name: General controller structure
skills.summary: Combine feedforward, state feedback and estimation into a 2-DOF structure.

skills.name: Equilibrium points and phase portraits
skills.summary: Find equilibria and sketch phase portraits of 2-D nonlinear systems.

skills.name: Linearization about an equilibrium
skills.summary: Compute Jacobians and use local linear models for analysis and control.

skills.name: Lyapunov stability
skills.summary: Prove stability with a Lyapunov function and the Lyapunov equation.

skills.name: Limit cycles, bifurcations and nonlocal behavior
skills.summary: Recognize limit cycles, regions of attraction and parameter bifurcations.

skills.name: Feedback linearization
skills.summary: Cancel nonlinearities with input transformations to get linear dynamics.

skills.name: Gain scheduling
skills.summary: Interpolate linear controllers designed at several operating points.

skills.name: System identification
skills.summary: Fit a model from step/frequency data and least squares.

skills.name: Model predictive control (intro)
skills.summary: Solve a receding-horizon optimization with constraints at each step.

skills.name: Adaptive control (intro)
skills.summary: Update controller parameters online from estimates.

skills.name: Applications tour: op-amps, AFM, drug dosing, populations
skills.summary: Apply modeling and feedback ideas to the textbook's application families.

skills.name: LTI analysis of RC and RLC circuits
skills.summary: Apply linearity, convolution and step response to circuit equations: RC charging, pulses, rise time and loading.

skills.name: Frequency response and transfer functions of circuits
skills.summary: Sinusoidal steady state of RC/RL filters, impedance magnitudes, voltage gain and transimpedance.

skills.name: Poles, zeros and Bode plots of circuits
skills.summary: Locate poles and zeros from circuit time constants and sketch Bode plots of filters and amplifiers.

skills.name: Feedback amplifiers: feedback factor and loop gain
skills.summary: Find f, the loop gain and the closed-loop gain of op-amp feedback circuits.

skills.name: Gain errors in feedback amplifiers
skills.summary: Static and dynamic gain errors of op-amp amplifiers from finite and frequency-dependent open-loop gain.

skills.name: Op-amp and amplifier stability and compensation
skills.summary: Phase margin of op-amp loops: second poles, capacitive loads, dominant-pole and Miller compensation.

skills.name: LTI models of mechanical systems
skills.summary: Mass-spring-damper and rotational systems as LTI models: static gain, natural frequency, damping, step and frequency response.

skills.name: Stability margins in control loop design
skills.summary: Use gain, phase, delay and sensitivity margins to judge and tune control loops.

skills.name: Formulating an optimization problem
skills.summary: Name the decision variable, the objective, and the feasible set, and tell a minimizer from the optimal value.

skills.name: Solving 2-D problems graphically
skills.summary: Lay objective contours over a planar feasible set and read off a minimizer.

skills.name: LP, QP, convex and nonlinear programs
skills.summary: Recognize linear, quadratic, convex, and general nonlinear programs.

skills.name: Support vector machines as a quadratic program
skills.summary: Turn a maximum-margin separator into a quadratic program in the weights.

skills.name: Key subsets of R^n
skills.summary: Describe orthants, simplices, lines, segments, hyperplanes, and half-spaces as subsets of R^n.

skills.name: Spectral decomposition of symmetric matrices
skills.summary: Diagonalize a real symmetric matrix with orthonormal eigenvectors and rebuild it from its eigenpairs.

skills.name: Positive (semi)definite matrices
skills.summary: Test positive semidefinite and definite matrices by eigenvalues, and read quadratic-form level sets as ellipses.

skills.name: Singular value decomposition
skills.summary: Factor a matrix as a rotation, an axis stretch, and a rotation, and read the rank from the singular values.

skills.name: Rayleigh quotient and eigenvalue bounds
skills.summary: Bound the Rayleigh quotient by the extreme eigenvalues, and use trace and determinant as their sum and product.

skills.name: Inner products
skills.summary: Use the inner-product axioms, the dot product, the Frobenius pairing, and orthogonality.

skills.name: Vector norms and l_p norms
skills.summary: Check the norm axioms and compare the 1-norm, 2-norm, and infinity-norm, including their unit balls.

skills.name: Cauchy-Schwarz inequality
skills.summary: Apply the bound on an inner product, including the equality case and the step that yields the triangle inequality.

skills.name: Induced matrix norms
skills.summary: Compute the operator norm and the closed forms of the matrix 1-norm, infinity-norm, and 2-norm.

skills.name: Frobenius and Schatten norms
skills.summary: Compute the Frobenius norm from entries or singular values, and name the nuclear and spectral norms as Schatten norms.

skills.name: Open and closed sets in R^n
skills.summary: Tell open and closed sets apart using balls, interior points, boundary, and closure.

skills.name: Bounded and compact sets
skills.summary: Use compactness in R^n as closed and bounded, and recognize standard sets that fail it.

skills.name: Sublevel sets and contour sets
skills.summary: Sketch sublevel sets and level curves of a simple function of several variables.

skills.name: Convex sets
skills.summary: Test convexity with line segments, and keep convexity under intersection.

skills.name: Directional derivative
skills.summary: Compute a directional derivative from its one-sided limit along a line.

skills.name: Partial derivatives and the gradient
skills.summary: Build the gradient from partial derivatives and use it as the direction of steepest increase.

skills.name: Differentiability in several variables
skills.summary: Use the linear-approximation definition of differentiability and separate it from the existence of partial derivatives.

skills.name: Second derivatives and the Hessian
skills.summary: Assemble second partial derivatives into the Hessian and use symmetry of mixed partials.

skills.name: Jacobian and multivariable chain rule
skills.summary: Multiply Jacobians to differentiate a composition, including the gradient of a scalar composition.

skills.name: Gradients of linear and quadratic forms
skills.summary: Differentiate c^T x, a squared norm, and x^T A x, including a nonsymmetric A.

skills.name: Fundamental theorem of calculus along a segment
skills.summary: Write a function increment and a gradient increment as integrals along the segment between two points.

skills.name: First- and second-order Taylor approximations
skills.summary: Build the linear and quadratic models of a function from its gradient and Hessian.

skills.name: Exact Taylor expansions and the mean value theorem
skills.summary: Place the remainder at an intermediate point and turn an expansion into a bound.

skills.name: Convex functions
skills.summary: Use the chord definition of convexity, including strict convexity, for norms and affine maps.

skills.name: First-order convexity condition
skills.summary: Use the tangent inequality as a global underestimator of a differentiable convex function.

skills.name: Second-order convexity test
skills.summary: Test convexity of a twice differentiable function by a positive semidefinite Hessian.

skills.name: Finite-difference derivatives
skills.summary: Choose between forward and central differences and balance truncation against round-off.

skills.name: Computational graphs
skills.summary: Break a formula into elementary steps and compare symbolic, numeric, and automatic differentiation.

skills.name: Forward-mode automatic differentiation
skills.summary: Push a tangent through a computational graph to get one directional derivative.

skills.name: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation
skills.summary: Sweep adjoints backward to get a full gradient at a cost close to one function evaluation.

skills.name: Hessian-vector products with automatic differentiation
skills.summary: Combine forward and reverse modes to apply the Hessian to a vector without forming the matrix.

skills.name: Backpropagation for a small neural network
skills.summary: Apply reverse-mode differentiation to the weights of a two-layer classifier loss.

skills.name: Local and global minimizers
skills.summary: Distinguish local and global minimizers, strict and non-strict, and a minimum from an infimum.

skills.name: Existence of minimizers
skills.summary: Use compactness or coercivity to decide whether a minimum is attained.

skills.name: First-order necessary condition
skills.summary: Set the gradient to zero at an interior local minimizer and name the stationary points.

skills.name: Second-order optimality conditions
skills.summary: Use a positive semidefinite Hessian as necessary and a positive definite Hessian as sufficient.

skills.name: Classifying stationary points
skills.summary: Find the stationary points of a simple function and classify them as minima, maxima, or saddles.

skills.name: Optimality for convex functions
skills.summary: Conclude that a stationary point of a convex function is a global minimizer.

skills.name: Minimizing quadratic functions
skills.summary: Solve a quadratic minimization from the linear system given by its Hessian, and tell when a solution exists.

skills.name: Linear programs and standard form
skills.summary: Rewrite a linear program with slack variables, split free variables, and clear absolute values.

skills.name: Graphical LP solution and solution types
skills.summary: Solve a planar linear program and recognize unique, multiple, unbounded, and infeasible cases.

skills.name: Polyhedra and extreme points
skills.summary: Identify vertices of a polyhedron with basic feasible solutions.

skills.name: Constructing basic feasible solutions
skills.summary: Choose a basis, solve for the basic variables, and check feasibility.

skills.name: Basic directions, reduced costs, and the ratio test
skills.summary: Build a feasible edge step from reduced costs and the largest step that stays nonnegative.

skills.name: The simplex method
skills.summary: Run one simplex iteration, including the tests for optimality and an unbounded ray.

skills.name: Finding an initial basic feasible solution
skills.summary: Build the auxiliary problem that either returns a basic feasible solution or proves infeasibility.

skills.name: Lagrangian lower bounds and the dual problem
skills.summary: Form the Lagrangian dual and use weak duality as a lower bound on the primal value.

skills.name: Lagrange multipliers for equality constraints
skills.summary: Write the Lagrange condition for equality constraints and see how it fails when constraint gradients are dependent.

skills.name: KKT conditions
skills.summary: Add nonnegative multipliers and complementary slackness for inequality constraints.

skills.name: LP duality from KKT
skills.summary: Derive the dual of a standard-form linear program from its KKT system.

skills.name: Projection onto affine sets and half-spaces
skills.summary: Project a point onto an affine set or a half-space with a short KKT calculation.

skills.name: Linear least squares
skills.summary: Solve an overdetermined linear fit by the normal equations when the columns are independent.

skills.name: Least-squares data fitting
skills.summary: Fit a model that is linear in its parameters, and count how many points the fit needs.

skills.name: Nonlinear least-squares problems
skills.summary: Write a nonlinear fit as a sum of squared residuals and form the residual Jacobian.

skills.name: Circle fitting by least squares
skills.summary: Rewrite a circle fit so that it becomes a linear least-squares problem.

skills.name: Descent directions
skills.summary: Test a direction by a negative directional derivative, including scaled gradients with a positive definite scaling.

skills.name: General descent methods
skills.summary: Separate the choice of direction, the step length, and the stopping test in a descent iteration.

skills.name: Rates of convergence
skills.summary: Classify linear, superlinear, sublinear, and quadratic convergence from a sequence of errors.

skills.name: Exact line search on quadratics
skills.summary: Compute the exact step length along a direction for a quadratic objective.

skills.name: Armijo backtracking line search
skills.summary: Check the sufficient-decrease inequality and see why backtracking eventually accepts a step.

skills.name: Zig-zagging of steepest descent
skills.summary: See why exact line search makes successive steepest-descent steps orthogonal, and why a large condition number zigzags.

skills.name: Condition number and gradient-descent rate
skills.summary: Bound the linear rate of steepest descent on a quadratic by the condition number.

skills.name: Lipschitz-continuous gradients
skills.summary: Bound the Lipschitz constant of a gradient by a Hessian operator norm.

skills.name: The descent lemma
skills.summary: Use the quadratic upper bound on a function with a Lipschitz gradient.

skills.name: Sufficient decrease lemma
skills.summary: Quantify the decrease of a gradient step whose length is below twice the reciprocal Lipschitz constant.

skills.name: Convergence of the gradient method
skills.summary: Conclude that gradient norms go to zero and name the sublinear rate for a smooth function.

skills.name: Gauss-Newton method
skills.summary: Linearize residuals and solve a linear least-squares subproblem at each step.

skills.name: Levenberg-Marquardt method
skills.summary: Damp a Gauss-Newton step so that it bends toward steepest descent when the linear model is poor.

skills.name: Incremental gradient methods
skills.summary: Replace the full gradient by a pass through data blocks, and compare the step-size behavior with batch descent.

skills.name: Kalman filter as recursive least squares
skills.summary: Derive the Kalman update as incremental Gauss-Newton on linear least-squares blocks.

skills.name: Extended Kalman filter
skills.summary: Relinearize a nonlinear measurement model on each new block.

skills.name: Newton's method for root finding
skills.summary: Solve a nonlinear equation by repeatedly linearizing it, and see the role of the start point.

skills.name: Newton's method for minimization
skills.summary: Step to the minimizer of the quadratic Taylor model, and see that the same step can be attracted to a maximum.

skills.name: Local quadratic convergence of Newton
skills.summary: Explain the local quadratic rate of Newton's method when the Hessian is Lipschitz and positive definite.

skills.name: Globalizing Newton's method
skills.summary: Add a line search or a Hessian shift so that a Newton step becomes a descent step.

skills.name: Wolfe line-search conditions
skills.summary: Pair sufficient decrease with a curvature condition so that the step satisfies a positive secant curvature.

skills.name: Quasi-Newton methods and the secant equation
skills.summary: Build a Hessian approximation that matches the gradient change along the last step.

skills.name: BFGS update
skills.summary: Apply the BFGS formula and keep it positive definite when the curvature condition holds.

skills.name: Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization
skills.summary: Orthogonalize independent vectors in a chosen inner product, including x^T Q y.

skills.name: Conjugate directions
skills.summary: Use Q-conjugacy so that exact line search on a quadratic finishes in finitely many steps.

skills.name: Conjugate gradient method
skills.summary: Generate conjugate directions from gradients and relate the rate to the condition number.

skills.name: Heavy-ball momentum
skills.summary: Add a momentum term to gradient descent and compare its rate with the plain gradient method.

skills.name: Nesterov's accelerated gradient
skills.summary: Extrapolate before the gradient step and distinguish the scheme from heavy-ball momentum.

skills.name: Optimality over a convex set
skills.summary: Use the variational inequality for a minimizer over a convex set, and see why convexity of the objective matters.

skills.name: Projection onto a convex set
skills.summary: Characterize the projection by an obtuse angle and compute it for simple convex sets.

skills.name: Gradient projection method
skills.summary: Write stationarity as a fixed point of a projected gradient step and run the iteration.

skills.name: Scaled gradient projection
skills.summary: Project in a scaled inner product, with projected Newton as one case.

skills.name: Affine scaling for linear programs
skills.summary: Follow a sequence of scaled quadratic models inside a linear program, in primal or dual form.

skills.name: Primal-dual interior-point methods
skills.summary: Take Newton steps on a perturbed KKT system and stay near the central path.

skills.name: Conditional gradient (Frank-Wolfe) method
skills.summary: Minimize a linear model over a simplex or an l1 ball and step toward that vertex.

skills.name: Power method for the top eigenvector
skills.summary: Read power iteration as conditional gradient on the Rayleigh quotient.
